key_insight: Clipped decentralized SGD can achieve order-optimal convergence under heavy-tailed noise while preserving linear speed-up across agents.
engineering_relevance: For distributed machine learning systems, gradient clipping offers a practical, baseline-safe way to stabilize training under heavy-tailed gradients without sacrificing scalability.
method: Use decentralized SGD with local gradient clipping under smooth non-convex objectives.
Analyze convergence for bounded p-th moment noise with p in (1, 2].
Derive sharp consensus-gap bounds showing network effects are higher-order terms.
evidence_signal: The paper reports order-optimal rates in both high-probability and expectation settings, plus numerical experiments that validate the theory.
watch_item: Clipping changes both optimization and consensus dynamics, so clip threshold tuning and network-dependent behavior still need careful implementation.
paper_title: Decentralized SGD under Heavy-Tailed Noise: Optimal Convergence Rates and the Role of Gradient Clipping
